title: Existence and quantity
grammar: There is/are, Some/Any, How much/How many
function: Describe what exists in a place

sections.heading: There is / There are
sections.body: We use 'there is' and 'there are' to say that something exists or is present. 'There is' is for singular, 'there are' for plural.
table: There is a cat on the sofa.
There are two books on the table.
Is there a bank near here?

sections.heading: Some and any
sections.body: We use 'some' in positive sentences and 'any' in negatives and questions. Both can be used with countable and uncountable nouns.
table: There is some milk. There are some apples.
There isn't any milk. There aren't any apples.
Is there any milk? Are there any apples?

sections.heading: How much / How many
sections.body: We use 'how much' with uncountable nouns and 'how many' with countable nouns.
table: How much money do you have?

sections.heading: Countable and uncountable nouns
sections.body: Countable nouns can be counted (one apple, two apples). Uncountable nouns cannot (water, rice, money).
list: Countable: apple, book, chair, friend, car, house
Uncountable: water, milk, rice, money, time, bread, cheese
We use 'a few' with countable and 'a little' with uncountable.
We use 'many' with countable and 'much' with uncountable.

sections.heading: Quantifiers
table: There are a lot of people.
I have a few friends here.

sections.heading: Common mistakes
list: Do not say 'There is two books'. Say 'There are two books'.
Do not use 'much' with countable nouns.
Do not use 'many' with uncountable nouns.
Remember: 'some' in positive, 'any' in negative and questions.

phases.name: Discovery
phases.intro: Look at these sentences. Read them carefully and think about the questions below.
sentences: There is a cat on the sofa.
There are two books on the table.
Is there any milk in the fridge?
There is some cheese on the plate.
How much money do you have?
There are a lot of people in the park.
questions: In sentences 1 and 2, when do we use 'there is' and when 'there are'?
In sentences 3 and 4, when do we use 'some' and when 'any'?
In sentences 6 and 7, what is the difference between 'how many' and 'how much'?
In sentence 8, why can we use 'a lot of' with both countable and uncountable?
Look at all the sentences: what type of noun follows 'much'? What type follows 'many'?

sections.heading: Key rules
list: There is + singular. There are + plural.
Some: positive sentences. Any: negatives and questions.
How much + uncountable. How many + countable.
A few + countable. A little + uncountable.
A lot of can be used with both countable and uncountable.

sections.heading: Common mistakes
list: Do not say 'There is two books'. Say 'There are two books'.
Do not use 'much' with countable nouns.
Do not use 'many' with uncountable nouns.
Remember: 'some' positive, 'any' negative and questions.

sections.heading: Useful phrases
list: There is a...
There are some...
Is there any...?
There isn't any...
How much...?
How many...?
A few, a little, a lot of.
